summary: The **application factory** that assembles the FastAPI app: logging, OpenAPI metadata, CORS and request-context middleware, a catch-all error handler, the `/api/v1` routers, the static frontend and the dashboard page. Its `lifespan` handler creates tables, seeds an empty database, connects the SSE hub to the event loop and stops live traffic on shutdown. The module-level `app` is what `python -m iip` serves through uvicorn and what the tests import.

notes.text: Module docstring: the application factory, which wires configuration, middleware, the API, the live hub and the dashboard page into one FastAPI app.
Deferred evaluation of type hints, as in the other modules.
`asyncio`, needed to grab the server's running event loop at startup.
Python's standard logging module.
`asynccontextmanager` turns an async generator function into an async context manager, the shape FastAPI expects for a lifespan handler.
`FastAPI` is the application class; `Request` types the error handler's first argument.
Middleware that answers browsers' cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) checks.
Response classes for a file, an HTML string and a JSON body.
`StaticFiles` serves a directory of files as-is; the `RevalidatingStaticFiles` subclass below adds a caching header for the frontend.
`select` and `func`, for the startup query that counts users.
The package version from `iip/__init__.py`, shown in the API docs.
`WEB_DIR` points at the `web/` folder; `settings` holds the environment-driven configuration from `config.py`.
The session factory, the `User` model for the emptiness check and `init_db` to create tables.

The two real-time singletons from `live.py`: `hub` fans messages out to browsers over Server-Sent Events (SSE, a one-way stream from server to browser over a long-lived HTTP response), and `traffic` is the optional live-traffic generator.
The middleware from `observability.py` that adds request IDs and timings and feeds the metrics.
One router bundling every API module under `/api/v1` (built in `routes/__init__.py`).
The seeder, used on first start.
Configures the root logger once, at import: INFO and above, each line showing time, level padded to 7 characters (`%(levelname)-7s` left-aligns it so messages line up), logger name and message.
The application's logger. Other modules use names like `iip.http` and `iip.live`, which makes them children of `iip` in Python's dotted logger hierarchy.

A tiny subclass of Starlette's `StaticFiles`. The JavaScript and CSS files have plain names (no content hash), and without a caching header a browser may reuse an old copy on reload, so after an update the page could run stale code. The docstring states the trade-off: revalidation costs one request per file, answered with a tiny `304 Not Modified` when nothing changed.
Overrides the hook `StaticFiles` calls to build each file's response, letting the parent do all the real work (paths, ETags, 304s).

`Cache-Control: no-cache` doesn't mean "don't cache": it means "cache, but check with the server before reusing", so updates appear on the next reload. The response is then returned unchanged otherwise.

`TAGS` is OpenAPI tag metadata: each entry gives a group of endpoints a description in the interactive docs at `/docs`, and the list order sets the order of the groups. Names must match the `tags=[...]` each router declares, here `events`, `incidents` and `users`.
The remaining groups: `risk engine`, `simulation` and `integration`. The `dashboard` and `ai analyst` routers aren't listed, so their groups appear without a description. Line 32 closes the list.

The **lifespan** handler (FastAPI's replacement for the older startup and shutdown events): code before `yield` runs once when the server starts, code after it once at shutdown. FastAPI passes in the app; naming the parameter `_` signals it is unused.
Creates any missing tables. `create_all` skips tables that already exist, so it is safe on every start.
Opens a short-lived database session; the `with` block guarantees it is closed.
If the `users` table is empty (`SELECT count(*) FROM users` returns 0), logs it and seeds the synthetic data. That is why a fresh checkout opens on a populated dashboard with no setup.
Hands the server's event loop to the SSE hub. Sync endpoints run in worker threads, and the hub needs this loop to pass their messages back safely (via `call_soon_threadsafe`).
The app serves requests while the lifespan is paused here.
On shutdown, cancels the live-traffic task if it is running. Startup never starts it; it is switched on from the Simulation Center (`POST /api/v1/simulation/traffic`).
The **application factory**: a function that builds and returns a fully configured app, keeping all the wiring in one place.
Creates the `FastAPI` instance with the title and version shown in the docs, the `lifespan` handler above and the tag metadata.
The description shown at the top of `/docs`; two adjacent string literals are joined into one. Line 52 closes the call.

Allows cross-origin requests only from the configured origins (by default `http://localhost:8000` and `http://127.0.0.1:8000`), only with the verbs the API uses, and with any header, so `X-API-Key` can be sent. The bundled dashboard is same-origin and doesn't need this; it matters for a frontend served from elsewhere.

Starlette wraps middleware so that the **last** one added is the outermost layer. Adding `RequestContextMiddleware` last means it sees each request first and each response last, so it can time and tag (`X-Request-ID`, `X-Response-Time`) everything inside it.
A catch-all handler for any exception nothing else handled. `HTTPException`s (404, 401, 429, ...) and validation errors (422) keep FastAPI's own handlers.
Logs the full traceback on the server; `log.exception` logs at ERROR level with the stack trace.
Returns a generic 500 JSON body, so internals such as stack traces or SQL never leak to the client.
Mounts all API routes under `/api/v1`.
Serves everything in `web/` (CSS, JavaScript, the vendored anime.js, the favicon) under `/static`, through the revalidating subclass so browsers always pick up the latest frontend code.

The dashboard page at `/`. `response_class=HTMLResponse` sends the returned string as HTML, and `include_in_schema=False` hides the route from the API docs (and from the endpoint catalog built from them).
Returns the page's HTML as a string.
Reads `index.html` fresh on every request, so edits show up on reload.
Comment flagging the trade-off: injecting the key is a demo convenience, not a security model (see the README's Security section).

Replaces the `__IIP_API_KEY__` placeholder (in a `<meta name="iip-api-key">` tag) with the real key in demo mode, or an empty string otherwise. `web/js/core/api.js` reads that tag; when it is empty, the user is asked for the key once per browser session.
Browsers request `/favicon.ico` automatically; this route answers it, also hidden from the docs.
Serves the SVG icon at that path with the correct `image/svg+xml` type instead of a 404.
Returns the configured app.
Builds the module-level `app` at import time. This is the object uvicorn loads as `"iip.app:app"` (see `__main__.py`) and the object the tests import.
